findings.title: Substring matching does not establish an errors-only query
findings.body: The presence of `event.type:error` anywhere in the raw query does not mean the query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects on Discover, these requests are consequently rewritten to aggregate `sample_weight` even though they select transactions, which this helper explicitly says do not have that field. This can produce incorrect counts or query failures. Determine eligibility from parsed query constraints rather than a substring.

findings.title: Top-event selection still uses the unweighted count
findings.body: Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed for top-events requests; `selected_columns` and `orderby` still come directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups by stored event count, then displays their weighted counts. With different client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest upsampled count and still be omitted from the chart. Apply consistent weighted aggregation to the top-group selection and ordering as well as the returned time series.

findings.title: Use the dataset and query actually being executed for eligibility
findings.body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and the original request query instead of `scoped_dataset` and the `query` passed to this invocation. The dashboard-splitting path explicitly calls this function with Discover and an errors-only query while the outer dataset is metrics-enhanced performance. The helper rejects that outer dataset, so counts for sampled error events remain unweighted in those dashboard results, including widgets already classified as error events. Base eligibility on the scoped execution context so these error queries receive the same upsampling as direct error queries.
